text:
incident-bot: Paging @sre_jordan — elevated error rate and latency on /v1/embeddings in ap-southeast-1 (alerts: 3xx -> 5xx spike, RPS +8x). Auto-escalation due to sustained>5m

sre_jordan: on it, looking at dashboards now. do we have a region-wide fanout? :eyes:

security_maya: I'm seeing a massive increase in unique client IPs hitting embeddings and stream endpoints, pattern looks like scraper farm (short sessions, many token lengths). WAF signals: repetitive user-agent patterns and cookie-less clients.

ops_emma: can we geo-throttle ap-southeast-1 while we triage? if we apply too broad a rule might affect legit customers.

sre_jordan: starting with a soft geo-shape + stricter rate limit on anonymous traffic. I'll push a temporary WAF rule flagged as 'temp-scraper-apac-2071' and add a 429 policy for suspect UA.

sre_jordan: running commands now:
```
# create temporary WAF block list
wafctl add-rule --name=temp-scraper-apac-2071 --match "ua:/(python-requests|curl|bot)/i" --action=block --region=ap-southeast-1
# throttle anonymous embed requests
redwoodctl policy apply --name=anon-embed-throttle --scope=public --region=ap-southeast-1 --rate=30r/s
```

ops_emma: ACK, rolling out to canary edge nodes then full region. Watch for 504s from overloaded origin when throttle hits.

support_natalie: heads-up: a few customers in APAC are already DMing support about timeouts. we should prepare a short customer-facing note.

product_ryan: agreed. short status: "We’re mitigating an automated scraper affecting embeddings in APAC. We’ve applied regional throttles and WAF rules — some customers may see increased latency or 429s. Working on recovery." Keep it high level.

sre_jordan: initial metrics: error rate down ~45% after WAF canary, RPS from top IPs dropped 10x. Overall latency for affected routes still 1.8-2.4s (baseline ~200ms). Some legitimate large-batch customers getting 429s — we need whitelist for known customers.

security_maya: preparing CIDR allowlist for customers that present API keys. suggest policy: API-keyed requests bypass geo throttle but still count against quota.

sre_jordan: applied allowlist for three known customers (IDs: cust-42, cust-87, cust-311). Command:
```
redwoodctl allowlist add --customer=cust-42 --routes=/v1/embeddings --region=ap-southeast-1
```

ops_emma: we also disabled the public batch endpoint for now to reduce load on the embedding workers. disabled: /v1/batch (public). internal/dedicated unaffected.

support_natalie: notified affected customers with id list and ETA: "we expect mitigation impact to stabilize in 30-60 minutes; if you're seeing continued errors please contact support with request-id and we'll route to SRE" :envelope_with_arrow:

product_ryan: product ask: can we enable finer-grained quotas rather than blunt geo throttle? i.e., short-term per-key token caps that don't block authenticated customers.

sre_jordan: doable — deploying per-key soft quotas now (limit 200k tokens/hour per key for anonymous/unverified). Command:
```
quotactl set --scope=key --policy=soft --limit=200000 --region=ap-southeast-1
```

security_maya: WAF logs show some probes are using distributed proxies; we should add rate limiting at the edge LB level too. coordinating with infra team.

ops_emma: infra confirmed edge-rate-limit rollout in progress. also spinning up 2 spare embed worker pods on the dedicated pool to reduce queuing for whitelisted keys.

sre_jordan: doing a handoff to @ops_emma for sustained monitoring — I'm off call in 20. Summary for handoff:
- Incident: scraper-driven embeddings surge from ap-southeast-1
- Actions taken: temporary WAF block rule (temp-scraper-apac-2071), geo soft-throttle, disabled public /v1/batch, allowlist for known customers, per-key soft quotas
- Current status: error rate down ~60% from peak, latency improved but still ~500-2000ms for some paths, dedicated pool scale up in progress
- Next steps: edge LB rate limits, keep WAF rule for 2-4 hours, prepare post-incident customer note if stable

ops_emma: taking over. will keep WAF in place and monitor for collateral. setting reminder to re-evaluate in 2h. please post a concise incident summary to #incidents-postmortems after we close.

support_natalie: I'll update the ticket queue and send a status update to affected customers. adding note: "Actions taken may temporarily return some 429s — we prioritized availability for authenticated customers."

product_ryan: status.redwood.ai draft ready. can someone from SRE approve wording? draft: "We observed an automated scraping event originating in APAC that impacted embeddings. We applied regional mitigations (WAF + throttles) and disabled a public batch route to protect service. Authenticated customers are prioritized and we are scaling dedicated capacity."

ops_emma: approved. go ahead and publish.

sre_jordan: logging runbook entries and tag incident with labels: abuse, waf, apac, embeddings. I'll follow up with metrics snapshot and retain WAF logs for 7 days.

incident-bot: Incident assigned -> channel #incidents/2071234567 (autocreated). Severity: S2. Owners: ops_emma, sre_jordan.

ops_emma: final note — re-enable /v1/batch (public) only after traffic normalizes and we've validated quotas for anonymous flows. will post update in ~90m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

support_natalie: thanks all, will keep customers looped in.

sre_jordan: thanks team. handing off now.
